items.summary: Security disposition is evidence_needed fleet-wide, with new public exposure and security-sensitive releases blocked pending evidence. Concrete evidence: the security fleet-doctor has no run or findings; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt readiness are therefore unverified. Compliance reports 36 pass, 19 fail, and 6 unknown across the technical baseline, while TLS evidence only confirms no certificates expiring within 30 days and does not establish complete TLS posture. Exact decision: preserve existing private-launch and security-sensitive release gates; permit ordinary reversible growth only when it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, cross-site behavior, or new public exposure.

Do not clear any security-sensitive release or new public exposure. Complete one consolidated read-only evidence matrix from authorized metadata and retained artifacts covering authentication/access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release/deploy controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, incident and monitoring signals, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, alter permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, or request duplicate telemetry.

items.title: Maintain evidence-needed fleet security disposition and release gates
items.summary: The fleet cannot receive a clean security clearance from the available evidence. Keep new public exposure and security-sensitive releases blocked while completing a bounded read-only control matrix. Ordinary reversible growth may continue conditionally when it does not expand authority, data collection, dependencies, credentials, permissions, or cross-site behavior.
items.requested_action: Maintain the existing private-launch and security-sensitive release gates. Produce one dated evidence matrix using only authorized metadata and retained artifacts, recording confirmed evidence, unknowns, affected scope, severity, owner, and release implication for each control area. Do not request duplicate telemetry or perform penetration testing. Permit ordinary reversible growth only if it preserves current consent, disclosures, data handling, claims, and access boundaries and does not introduce credentials, permissions, dependencies, new data collection, or public exposure.
